applies_why: The judge is resolving a collision over Acts 2:30 by resting on the cited text's silence about whose body is the channel, so K-C governs whether that may be done verse by verse.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': one reading requires comparing the chains' footing, while the other permits noting that a single cited verse leaves the channel unnamed.
why: By making the single verse's failure to name the channel decisive for underdetermination, the judge uses a verse-level silence test rather than weighing the two chains by footing as K-C requires.
